title: Commit the DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS driver validate used, with stop, throw and close modes, under tests/window
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

in-process-click-respects-disabled-and-hidden: needs first: The committed stop mode has to check the control's state itself before it clicks: refuse when CancelButton.IsEnabled or IsVisible is false, so the C-006 case fails against a disabled or …
throw-mode-exit-70-comes-from-the-app: Own-built exe+hook: 10/10 exit 70, handler removed 3/3 0xE0434352; but 70 leaves no report

Mutation proofs live in validate's record (scratch copies, nothing committed) rather than in a committed script that applies the disabled, collapsed, handler-removed and Exit-rule-removed mutants. That is cheaper now, but it leaves the fail-ability proof outside the repo, which is the shape this slice exists to fix.
One Pressable gate on CancelButton for all three modes, even though throw does not logically need Stop. Per-mode triggers would be more precise. One gate is simpler and puts every fault mid-scan.
The closed-early case is named O-016 (an obligation) beside C-xxx criteria, and the hook project is FsaWindowHook under tests/window, not tests/window/hook. Both are naming and placement.
The hook reports through a text log file (FSA_HOOK_LOG). Stdout and a named event are the alternatives; the exe is WinExe with no console, which is why a file was chosen.
The inert-host assertion lives as a first step inside Test-C006, not as its own case ID.
SetErrorMode(SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX|SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) in throw mode. It is blocked by the existing InteropLivesOnlyInNative rule, and measured here as not needed; see deviations.

A person should decide whether InteropLivesOnlyInNative should exempt tests/window/FsaWindowHook, so the hook can call SetErrorMode on machines where WER shows a crash dialog. Today a regressed crash handler on such a machine fails C-012 as TIMEOUT rather than 0xE0434352.

Validate's O-013 (the hook cannot produce the outcome) can be measured with `WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant NoCrashHandler` and `-Mutant NoExitRule`. O-014 (the hook meets the user's gate) can be measured with `-Mutant StopDisabled`, `-Mutant StopCollapsed` and C-006's no-scan step. The design's 30-run repeat of stop and close against the committed hook has not been done: I ran each hooked case 3 to 4 times.

C-006 spends about 20 s waiting out the hook's fixed deadline in the no-scan step. If suite time matters, a shorter deadline for that one launch would need a contract addition, such as an FSA_HOOK_DEADLINE variable.
HookLocked stands in for 'dll locked by a leftover FsAnalyser.App.exe' with a FileStream that allows reading only. A real leftover app process with the dll mapped was not exercised.
HookLocked's output is noisy: MSBuild prints its 10 MSB3026 copy retries twice. The build output could be filtered to its error lines when Update-Hook fails.

deviation: Some wiring is shaped differently from the design. Invoke-HookedRun launches through Start-App and Wait-App (60 s), not eng/read-window.ps1: read-window picks its own report path, so no stale report …

drift: No new departures: the four the builder listed (the committed WindowMutants.ps1 runner, SetErrorMode dropped, three extra Test-C006 steps, Start-App/Wait-App wiring with $HookDll as a script constant…

not reached: A real input-driven press (mouse or UIA) on a CancelButton whose handler throws. O-015's premise, that a real click would reach DispatcherUnhandledException and exit 70, is reasoning about WPF, not something I measured.

not reached: A machine where Windows Error Reporting shows a crash dialog: with SetErrorMode dropped, a regressed crash handler there would show C-012 as TIMEOUT rather than 0xE0434352. Here the process ended at once.
not reached: Windows 10. Everything ran on Windows 11 26200 only.
not reached: Other .NET hosts inheriting the hook variables (dotnet.exe, MSBuild nodes). Only pwsh 7.6.6 on .NET 10.0.12 was checked. Update-Hook builds before any variable is set.
not reached: Slower or faster disks and CPUs. The hook acted at 336-917 ms with the scan at 550-750 of 30,150 folders here. On a much faster machine the margin before the scan finishes is unmeasured.
not reached: Any real user data or drive. Every run used generated trees under %TEMP%, which is why contact is graded code, not real.
